content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently underestimate early price spikes and overestimate later declines.", "Sentiment spikes correlate with forecast overshoots, especially in the first 5 days of the 30-day window.", "Model bias toward gradual increases masks sharp volatility in true outcomes, particularly after 15 days.", "Forecast lag is most pronounced when sentiment is neutral or negative, leading to delayed price corrections.", "True outcomes often exhibit mean-reversion after initial surges, contradicting model’s upward trend assumptions.", "Model accuracy improves when sentiment history includes at least one positive signal before the forecast window.", "Forecast models fail to capture sudden downward corrections when sentiment remains flat or negative for 3+ days.", "Sentiment history with zero values correlates with forecast underperformance, especially in the first 10 days of the 30-day window."]}
